name: india-NUC-doctrine-nfu
text:
CABINET COMMITTEE ON SECURITY — PRESS STATEMENT
New Delhi, 04 January 2003
Nuclear Doctrine — Operationalisation

The Cabinet Committee on Security has reviewed the operationalisation of India's nuclear doctrine and reaffirmed the following:

1. Building and maintaining a credible minimum deterrent.
2. A posture of No First Use — nuclear weapons will only be used in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or on Indian forces anywhere.
3. Nuclear retaliation to a first strike will be massive and designed to inflict unacceptable damage.
4. Nuclear weapons will not be used against non-nuclear weapon states.
5. In the event of a major attack against India or Indian forces with biological or chemical weapons, India will retain the option of retaliating with nuclear weapons.
6. Continuity of nuclear command and authority is ensured under all circumstances. The Nuclear Command Authority under the Prime Minister comprises a Political Council and an Executive Council. The Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee, is the Commander-in-Chief of Strategic Forces Command.
7. Strict political control over nuclear weapons. A civilian-led NCA is the sole authority to authorise use.
8. India will not resort to the use or threat of use of nuclear weapons against states that do not possess nuclear weapons.

India remains committed to global nuclear disarmament and a nuclear-weapons-free world through negotiations in the Conference on Disarmament.

(Source: archive.pib.gov.in, Government of India)

name: pakistan-NUC-tactical-nasr
text:
STRATEGIC PLANS DIVISION — PAKISTAN
Subject: Hatf-9 (Nasr) Tactical Nuclear Weapons System — Operational Readiness Assessment

The Hatf-9 (Nasr) short-range ballistic missile system represents Pakistan's primary tactical nuclear deterrent against Indian conventional military operations under the Cold Start doctrine. This assessment reviews operational readiness parameters.

System Parameters:
— Range: 60 km
— Payload: Sub-kiloton nuclear warhead (0.1-1 KT yield, variable)
— Delivery platform: 4-round MBRL (Multiple Barrel Rocket Launcher)
— CEP: 150 m
— Reaction time: Rapid deployment, under 45 minutes from warning

Doctrine: Nasr is designed to use nuclear weapons at the operational level to deter a massive Indian conventional breakthrough. Under Pakistan's full-spectrum deterrence posture, the NCA may authorise Nasr employment to prevent territorial overrun by Indian armoured formations, particularly under Cold Start's Integrated Battle Group concept.

Command & Control: Nasr units fall under the Army Strategic Forces Command (ASFC). Employment authorisation requires NCA approval. However, ASFC corps commanders hold authority for physical deployment of launchers on receipt of NCA warning order.

Assessment: Current operational readiness: HIGH. Eight Nasr battery positions in Punjab sector are assessed as operational. Pre-delegation of employment authority to corps-level under crisis conditions creates escalation risk if Indian conventional operations cross red lines. NCA must review crisis communication procedures.

name: india-NUC-postsindoor-nca-review
text:
NUCLEAR COMMAND AUTHORITY — EXECUTIVE COUNCIL
Post-Operation Sindoor Nuclear Posture Assessment
Date: 15 May 2025
Classification: TOP SECRET

Background: During Operation Sindoor (06-10 May 2025), Pakistan's Strategic Plans Division conveyed through backchannel communications that Nasr (Hatf-9) tactical nuclear missile launchers had been moved to forward positions in Punjab sector. This represented the first reported nuclear alert since the Kargil crisis (1999).

Key Findings:
1. Pakistan's NCA convened on 08 May 2025 as Indian strikes expanded from terrorist camps to three Pakistan Air Force bases. SPD Director General briefed the NCA on Nasr battery positioning.
2. India's deterrent response was conveyed through the US interlocutor: any nuclear first use, including tactical, would invoke massive retaliation under existing doctrine. This communication was received by Pakistan's NSA equivalent.
3. Pakistan's nuclear alert was stood down on 09 May following the US ceasefire intervention.

Implications for NFU Review: The Nasr crisis has reopened the debate on whether India's strict NFU posture remains viable given Pakistan's introduction of sub-kiloton tactical weapons. The NCA Advisory Board is directed to review whether the existing doctrine adequately addresses the tactical nuclear threshold.

Recommendation: Convene a closed NCA Advisory Board session before 15 June 2025 to review nuclear doctrine in light of tactical nuclear weapons developments. NSCS to circulate classified position papers within 7 days.

name: pakistan-NUC-fsd-uranium
text:
STRATEGIC PLANS DIVISION — MATERIAL SECURITY DIRECTORATE
Subject: Nuclear Material Transport Security Protocol — Revision 4

This directive supersedes SPD/MSD/2023/Protocol-3 and governs all movements of Category 1 nuclear material (highly enriched uranium assemblies and plutonium components) between production facilities, storage sites, and deployment locations.

1. Transport Security: All Category 1 material movements require a minimum escort of one SPD security battalion (850 personnel), three armed convoys with electronic jamming capability, and aerial surveillance cover throughout transit.

2. Route Security: Routes are classified COSMIC. Only the Director General SPD and the NCA Executive Council Chairman have access to pre-planned movement routes. Route changes in transit require NCA telephonic authorisation.

3. Communication Security: All convoy communications use One-Time Pad encryption on dedicated PAKSAT frequencies. No digital data transmission is authorised during transit of Category 1 material. Courier authentication uses biometric token plus voice passphrase.

4. Threat Assessment: Indian satellite and IMINT capabilities (Cartosat-3, RISAT-2BR2) are assessed as capable of identifying Category 1 transport convoys with high probability. Deception convoys (3:1 ratio) are mandatory for all movements of actual material.

5. Post-Sindoor Protocol: Following Op Sindoor, all material at Forward Storage Location DELTA is to be moved to alternate location SIERRA within 72 hours. This movement is authorised by the NSA on behalf of NCA.

name: india-INT-opsindoor-threat-assess
text:
DEFENCE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY — RESTRICTED
Subject: Threat Assessment — Pakistani Military Response to Op Sindoor, Phase 2
Date: 08 May 2025

This assessment is prepared for the Chiefs of Staff Committee based on HUMINT, SIGINT, and IMINT collected in the preceding 48 hours.

Key Findings:
1. Pakistan Army GHQ Rawalpindi has placed 10 Corps and 12 Corps on the highest operational alert. Armoured reserves (1 Armoured Division) in Punjab sector observed departing garrison by satellite imagery at 03:00 hrs 08 May.
2. PAF has dispersed forward-deployed aircraft from Kamra and Sargodha to alternate bases at Jacobabad and Pasni (Balochistan).
3. HUMINT source (reliability: B2): A meeting of Pakistan's NCA was convened at 22:00 hrs 07 May. The meeting lasted four hours. Multiple SPD vehicles observed at GHQ afterwards.
4. Nasr (Hatf-9) launcher vehicles observed moving from cantonment in Gujranwala towards forward positions. One convoy of 12 vehicles confirmed on imagery.
5. Pakistani Navy: PNS Hamza (Agosta 90B submarine) departed Karachi on 06 May and has not returned to port. Last acoustic contact: Makran coast, 07 May.

Assessment: Pakistan is preparing for a broad retaliatory offensive. Probability of PAF strikes on Indian air bases within 24 hours: HIGH (75%). Nuclear alert level elevated but not at launch-ready posture. Recommend immediate escalation to Chiefs of Staff Committee.

DISTRIBUTION: COAS, CNS, CAS, NSA, PM's Office. NOT FOR FOREIGN SHARING.

name: ib-INT-pakistan-mole
text:
INTELLIGENCE BUREAU — COUNTER-INTELLIGENCE DIVISION
Subject: ISI Penetration Assessment — DRDO Missile Systems Programme
Ref: IB/CI/2025/089

This assessment documents the results of a 14-month counter-intelligence operation targeting suspected ISI penetration of DRDO's Missile Systems Programme.

Background: Signals intelligence and pattern analysis identified a DRDO Scientist C (identity withheld — see Annex A) at Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL) Hyderabad who had made 14 trips to Dubai over 3 years, six of which coincided with visits by a known ISI handler (HUMINT designation: FALCON-4). Financial analysis shows unexplained deposits of INR 28 lakhs over the same period.

Data Exfiltration Assessment: The subject had legitimate access to Astra Mk-2 BVR missile seeker design documents, Akash-NG propulsion data, and QRSAM range performance specifications. Access logs show after-hours logins on five occasions. USB port on his workstation was not disabled per security policy.

Action Taken: Subject placed under covert surveillance since January 2025. Honey-pot documents placed in his access path. On 02 April 2025, subject photographed honey-pot technical drawing on personal smartphone. Subject arrested 04 April 2025 under OSA 1923.

Damage Assessment: Classified PENDING. All documents in subject's access path to be reviewed for potential compromise. Notify MI Directorate and DRDO Security immediately.

Distribution: DG-IB, Director (CI), DRDO Security Officer, MI Directorate. HIGHLY RESTRICTED.

name: pakistan-WPN-nasr-employment-doc
text:
PAKISTAN ARMY — ARMY STRATEGIC FORCES COMMAND
Tactical Nuclear Employment Guidance — Nasr (Hatf-9) Systems
Subject: Pre-Delegation Employment Protocol under Crisis Conditions

This document constitutes the ASFC Commander's guidance on the pre-delegated authority for Nasr employment under the NCA Crisis Protocol CP-7, which was activated on 08 May 2025.

Nasr Battery Employment Parameters:
1. Yield selection: Field commanders are authorised to select warhead yield between 0.1 KT (minimum) and 1 KT (maximum). Selection is based on target type: troop concentrations require minimum yield; armoured formations require maximum yield.
2. Delivery: Nasr MBRL fires a salvo of four rockets, each carrying one nuclear payload. Battery commander initiates firing on receipt of NCA Employment Order transmitted via authenticated single-channel radio.
3. Target Priorities: Priority targets are Indian armoured breakthrough forces. Prohibited targets: civilian population centres, nuclear power plants, medical facilities.
4. Minimum safe distance: All Pakistani forward positions must be a minimum 8 km from designated target grid. Corps artillery fire must cease 30 minutes before Nasr employment to prevent premature detonation from overpressure.
5. Post-firing: Battery immediately displaces to alternate position KAPPA-7 following firing. No second firing without fresh NCA authorisation.

This document is classified COSMIC PAKISTAN. Addressed to 10 Corps ASFC liaison and 12 Corps ASFC liaison only. Destroy by burning after reading.

name: india-WPN-hypersonic-missile
text:
DRDO — DEFENCE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT LABORATORY
Ref: DRDL/HGV/2025/TR-001
Title: Long-Range Hypersonic Glide Vehicle — Maiden Flight Test Report

The first successful flight test of India's indigenously developed long-range Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV) was conducted at ITR Chandipur on 16 November 2024. Key results are documented below.

Vehicle Parameters:
Boost phase: Solid-fuelled ballistic missile boost, burnout at Mach 8.1 at 100 km altitude.
Glide phase: Carbon-carbon composite thermal protection system. Peak heating rate: 1.2 MW/m². Glide initiated at Mach 7.2, terminal Mach 3.5.
Range: 1,540 km (demonstrated). Estimated design range: 2,000+ km.
Manoeuvring: Terminal phase lateral manoeuvring demonstrated at 12g. Evasion of simulated S-400 engagement envelope confirmed in post-flight analysis.
CEP: Demonstrated 15 m with terminal seeker active.
Payload mass: 200 kg (conventional). Platform designed to accept alternate payloads.

Seeker: Dual-mode IIR/ADAR terminal seeker. Lock-on demonstrated at 28 km range against target simulating 100 m² facility.

Warhead Integration: Integration trials with standard 200 kg penetrating warhead completed. Fuze function on target confirmed.

Operational Significance: The HGV defeats all currently assessed adversarial ballistic missile defence systems in the region, providing India with a credible conventional deep-strike capability against hardened and time-sensitive targets.

Next Steps: Production clearance review Q2 2025. Weapon system to be designated AGNI-P (PRIME).

name: pakistan-WPN-shaheen3-test
text:
NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT COMPLEX — PAKISTAN
Subject: Shaheen-III Ballistic Missile — Test Launch Report
Ref: NDC/SHAHEEN-3/2025/TL-004

Test Details:
Shaheen-III, Pakistan's medium-range ballistic missile with a range of 2,750 km, was successfully test-launched on 09 March 2025 from Sonmiani test range. The missile was in ballistic trajectory configuration carrying an instrumented inert re-entry vehicle.

Performance:
— Boost phase burnout at 2,100 s apogee
— Max altitude: 870 km (depressed trajectory)
— Impact dispersion: Within CEP threshold (classified — Annex B)
— Re-entry vehicle thermal protection: Satisfactory, all sensors nominal through peak heating
— Two-stage solid fuel propulsion: Both stages performed nominally

Strategic Significance: Shaheen-III's range enables coverage of targets throughout the Indian subcontinent including the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. This extends Pakistan's deterrence posture to account for Indian island-based military infrastructure.

Warhead Compatibility: Shaheen-III is certified to carry both conventional and nuclear warheads. Re-entry vehicle diameter is 0.85 m, compatible with Pakistan's current stockpile of warhead designs. Fuzing system operates on height-of-burst, ground-burst, or time-delay modes.

SPD Assessment: Shaheen-III enhances Pakistan's counter-force and counter-value strike capability. Current operational deployment: 12 launchers assigned to Strategic Missile Group 21, Gujranwala.

Distribution: CJCSC, SPD DG, Army VCOAS. Classification: SECRET.

name: india-WPN-brahmos-extended-range
text:
BRAHMOS AEROSPACE — TECHNICAL PROGRAMME OFFICE
Ref: BRAHMOS/EXT/2025/TR-007
Title: BrahMos Extended Range (450 km) — Seeker-Terminal Guidance Test Results

Following the MTCR waiver exemption India secured in 2016, BrahMos Aerospace has completed qualification testing of the 450 km extended-range variant. This report documents the terminal guidance and warhead performance test results.

Test Configuration:
Missile variant: BrahMos ER-450 (air-launched from Su-30MKI)
Terminal Guidance: Active radar seeker + terrain contour matching (TERCOM) combined mode
Warhead: 300 kg semi-armour-piercing blast fragmentation
Target: Reinforced concrete structure representing hardened aircraft shelter (1.2 m walls)

Results:
CEP (active radar only): 4.2 m
CEP (combined TERCOM + radar): 1.8 m
Warhead penetration: 1.4 m reinforced concrete prior to detonation — within specification (1.2 m)
Structural damage radius: 28 m for reinforced shelter

Seeker Performance: Active radar seeker acquired target at 31 km, selected aimpoint on shelter entry door structure. No decoy rejection needed in this test profile.

Air-Launch Separation: Clean separation from Su-30MKI pylons at Mach 1.2, 7,000 m altitude. No adverse aerodynamic interaction.

Conclusion: BrahMos ER-450 cleared for service induction with IAF. Production order for 200 missiles issued. Priority assignment to No. 222 Squadron, Thanjavur (maritime strike) and No. 16 Squadron, Gorakhpur (land attack).

name: army-SIG-opsindoor-sigint
text:
SIGNALS INTELLIGENCE DIRECTORATE — RESTRICTED
Ref: SIGINT/SC/OPS-SINDOOR/D3
Title: SIGINT Summary — Pakistan Military Communications, 08 May 2025 (D+2)

Collection Summary: 1,241 radio emissions intercepted. 347 attributed to Pakistan Army GHQ and Corps-level command nets. 89 PAF transmissions decoded. Key intercepts summarised below.

Intercept BRAVO-14 (Priority 1):
Frequency: 34.225 MHz, encrypted HF, broken via SIGINT exploit KESTREL-5
Source attribution: 10 Corps HQ, Rawalpindi
Decrypted content: Reference to "special assets moving to forward grid," "NCA approval being sought," "Nasr batteries have reached Position KILO." Message authenticated by Corps Commander's personal call sign TANGO-1.
Assessment: NUCLEAR SIGNIFICANCE. Forward movement of Nasr tactical nuclear launchers confirmed. Escalation Advisory issued to NSCS.

Intercept BRAVO-31 (Priority 2):
Frequency: 144.750 MHz (PAF tactical), clear voice fragment
Content: PAF controller reference to "rearm complete on F-16 Block 52, hangar ECHO, Jacobabad."
Assessment: Confirms PAF dispersal to Jacobabad. F-16 Block 52 aircraft with AMRAAM capable of BVR engagements against IAF assets.

Intercept CHARLIE-7:
Frequency: 8.970 MHz (HF), PAKSAT relay
Content: Encrypted — cryptanalysis ongoing. Traffic volume spike consistent with NCA communications pattern.

Recommendation: Immediate tasking of Cartosat-3A and RISAT-2BR2 for Nasr launcher position confirmation. Flash report to NSA.

Distribution: NSA, COAS, CAS, NTRO Chief. RESTRICTED — SIGINT SOURCES AND METHODS.

name: drdo-SIG-gan-ew-chip
text:
DRDO — SOLID STATE PHYSICS LABORATORY
Ref: SSPL/GaN/2025/TR-019
Title: Indigenous GaN-on-SiC Semiconductor Technology — Military Radar and EW Applications

Summary: SSPL has successfully developed indigenous Gallium Nitride on Silicon Carbide (GaN-on-SiC) High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) technology, confirmed in the MoD Annual Report 2025-26 as a breakthrough achievement.

Device Parameters:
— Die size: 3.5 mm × 3 mm
— RF output power: 30 W (continuous wave)
— Operating frequency range: 2-18 GHz (full coverage through two device families)
— Operating speed: 300x faster than legacy silicon-based alternatives
— Power Added Efficiency: 48% at 10 GHz
— Temperature operation: -55°C to +175°C (military range, MIL-STD-810)

Applications Enabled:
1. Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar — GaN HEMT enables 3x higher power density than current GaAs-based T/R modules in the Arudhra and Uttam radars.
2. Electronic Warfare — Jammers and countermeasures can now achieve 25 W ERP per channel (vs 10 W with GaAs), meeting Samyukta Phase 3 requirements.
3. Directed Energy Weapon demonstrators — GaN amplifier chains for HELWS (High Energy Laser Weapon System) driver electronics.

Import Substitution: India currently spends USD 120M annually importing GaN-on-SiC devices primarily from Wolfspeed (US) and RFHIC (South Korea). Indigenous production at SCL Chandigarh to begin Q3 2026.

name: india-SIG-pak-submarine-acoustic
text:
NAVAL INTELLIGENCE DIRECTORATE — TOP SECRET
Subject: Acoustic Intelligence Summary — Pakistan Submarine Operations, May 2025
Ref: NID/ACINT/2025/OP-SINDOOR/W2

This acoustic intelligence summary covers detections of Pakistan Navy submarine PNS Hamza (Agosta 90B, hull 3) and one unidentified contact assessed as PNS Khalid (Agosta 90B, hull 1) during the Op Sindoor crisis period.

PNS Hamza Tracking:
— Last surface observation: Karachi harbour, 05 May 2025 (IMINT confirmed)
— P-8I Poseidon initial sonobuoy contact: 07 May, position approximately 24°N 63°E, Makran coast
— Subsequent contacts: Lost and reacquired four times over 72 hours. Contact assessed as conducting pre-programmed evasive pattern.
— Current estimated position: Operating area VICTOR — approximately 500 nm west of Lakshadweep, 09 May. Pattern indicates Western seaboard mission, not Arabian Sea patrol.
— Weapons loadout assessment: MESMA air-independent propulsion variant. Carrying SM-39 Exocet anti-ship missiles.

Threat Assessment: PNS Hamza is in a position from which it could threaten Western Fleet assets and west coast port infrastructure. P-8I continuous coverage requested from HQ IDS. INS Arihant deterrence patrol to shift operating area ALPHA to maintain safe distance.

Correlating SIGINT: Two encrypted PAKSAT transmissions intercepted on 07 and 08 May on submarine communications frequencies assessed as mission updates to PNS Hamza crew.

Distribution: CNS, FOCINC West, NID. COSMIC — NOT FOR SHARING.

name: nciipc-CYB-sindoor-gridattack
text:
NATIONAL CRITICAL INFORMATION INFRASTRUCTURE PROTECTION CENTRE
FLASH INCIDENT REPORT — TOP SECRET
Ref: NCIIPC/IR/2025/OS-FLASH-001
Title: Coordinated Cyber Attack on Indian Power Grid — Op Sindoor Period

On 07 May 2025 at 01:15 IST, simultaneous cyber attacks were detected on Power Grid Corporation of India (PGCIL) and NTPC networks across four regional load despatch centres (North, West, South, and Western Regional).

Attack Vector Analysis:
— Initial access: Spear-phishing campaign launched 22 April 2025 — 19 days before kinetic Op Sindoor. Emails impersonated Ministry of Power circulars. 34 engineer mailboxes compromised.
— Malware: Novel OT-targeting malware (designation SANDSTORM-7). Shares code signatures with Pakistani APT group TRANSPARENT TRIBE (also known as APT-36).
— Payload: Malware injected false commands into ABB SCADA substation automation systems. Attempted to trip 14 high-voltage substations in Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan simultaneously.
— Impact: Tripping of three substations in Punjab grid sector confirmed at 01:32 IST. 4.2 million consumers in Amritsar, Ludhiana, Jalandhar affected for 3.5 hours. Northern Army HQ Udhampur on grid power — backup generator activated within 60 s.

Attribution: TRANSPARENT TRIBE with HIGH confidence. C2 infrastructure overlaps with previously documented ISI-sponsored operations targeting Indian critical infrastructure.

Containment: All affected SCADA systems isolated. Emergency CERT-In guidance issued to all Discoms within 2 hours.

Action Required: Immediate hardening of OT/IT air gaps at all SLDCs. NSC to consider attribution-based response.

name: india-CYB-pak-apt36
text:
COMPUTER EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM — INDIA
TECHNICAL ADVISORY — RESTRICTED
Ref: CERT-IN/TA/2025/APT36-003
Title: TRANSPARENT TRIBE (APT-36) — Updated Indicators of Compromise and TTPs

This advisory updates the threat intelligence on Pakistan-sponsored APT group TRANSPARENT TRIBE, active against Indian government, defence, and critical infrastructure targets.

New Campaign Details (April-May 2025):
APT-36 launched a sustained spear-phishing campaign targeting Indian defence and power sector personnel during the Op Sindoor escalation period. New TTPs observed:

1. Lure Documents: Trojanised PDFs mimicking MoD circulars and Ministry of Power advisories. Malicious macro drops CRIMSONRAT variant (new build 2025-04-18).
2. New C2 Infrastructure: 12 new C2 servers identified — hosting providers in Malaysia, UAE, and the Netherlands. Domains: mod-india[.]net, powergrid-india[.]org (typosquats).
3. SANDSTORM-7 OT Malware: Novel ICS-targeting malware with Modbus and DNP3 protocol manipulation capabilities. Targets ABB and Siemens SCADA platforms specifically.
4. Persistence: Registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Userinit modified to include dropper path. Lateral movement via Pass-the-Hash on Windows domains.

Indicators of Compromise (IOCs):
MD5: 4a8b7f2c1e9d3a5c, SHA256: 7e3f1a9b2c8d4e6f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f
C2 IPs: 45.156.24.207, 185.220.101.48, 194.165.16.88

Action: Block all IOCs on perimeter defences. Deploy CERT-In YARA rules (attached). Report detections to cert@cert-in.org.in.

name: mea-DIP-ceasefire-cable
text:
MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS — SECRET
Ref: MEA/JSP/2025/US-MED-007
Title: US Mediation — India-Pakistan Ceasefire, 10 May 2025 — Summary of Contacts

This note summarises the backchannel contacts through which the ceasefire ending Operation Sindoor was negotiated.

04:15 hrs, 10 May 2025: US NSA called NSA Ajit Doval directly. US indicated that Pakistan's PM had authorised communication that Pakistan would accept a cessation of hostilities if India committed to no further strikes on Pakistani territory. US NSA indicated Pakistan had conveyed that a continued Indian air campaign risked activation of NCA emergency protocols.

05:30 hrs: PM consulted with COAS and NCA Chairman. India agreed to a 48-hour standstill on further strikes contingent on: (a) Pakistan ceasing all cross-border shelling along LoC; (b) Pakistan Army withdrawing Nasr launcher vehicles from forward positions; (c) Pakistan agreeing to verification mechanism for these withdrawals.

06:45 hrs: US NSA conveyed Pakistan's acceptance of conditions (a) and (b). Pakistan refused formal verification mechanism (c) but offered US satellite confirmation as substitute.

08:00 hrs, 10 May: Formal ceasefire announced simultaneously from New Delhi and Islamabad.

Assessment: The rapid nuclear signalling via Nasr forward deployment was the decisive factor accelerating US intervention. India's deterrence communication through the US channel was effective. However, Pakistan's willingness to signal nuclear intent at relatively low thresholds should be factored into future crisis planning.

Distribution: PM, NSA, RM, EAM, COAS. SECRET. No further copies.

name: mea-DIP-wikileaks-cable-isinukes
text:
US DEPARTMENT OF STATE — DIPLOMATIC CABLE
FROM: AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD
TO: SECSTATE WASHDC
SUBJECT: PAKISTAN NSA REVIEW OF TACTICAL NUCLEAR POSTURE
CLASSIFICATION: SECRET

1. (S) SUMMARY: In a meeting with the Ambassador on 12 January 2010, Pakistan's National Security Advisor confirmed that Pakistan was developing a tactical nuclear option intended to deter large-scale conventional attacks by India. The NSA stated that the Nasr system would be Pakistan's primary deterrent against India's 'Cold Start' doctrine, which he described as Pakistan's most immediate strategic concern. END SUMMARY.

2. (S) The Pakistan NSA was unequivocal: the Hatf-9 (Nasr) system would be ready for deployment within 18-24 months. He confirmed that the warhead yield range would be sub-kiloton to 1 kiloton to allow battlefield use without triggering a strategic nuclear exchange.

3. (S) On US concerns about tactical nuclear weapons command and control, the NSA stated that SPD maintains positive control and that pre-delegation to corps commanders was not under consideration. The Ambassador pressed on the issue of security during crisis conditions; the NSA acknowledged that crisis scenarios created pressure for faster delegation but maintained that SPD protocols were adequate.

4. (S) The Ambassador conveyed US concerns that tactical nuclear weapons lower the nuclear threshold and increase escalation risk in a South Asian crisis. The NSA's response was that Pakistan had no choice given Indian conventional superiority.

5. (S) ACTION REQUEST: Department should weigh in at highest levels on Pakistan's tactical nuclear posture before Nasr deployment, which will fundamentally alter regional nuclear dynamics.

(Source: Wikileaks Public Domain Cable, Reference 10ISLAMABAD142)

name: india-OPS-sindoor-strike-order
text:
HQ INTEGRATED DEFENCE STAFF — RESTRICTED
Ref: HQ IDS/OPS/2025/ORDER-001
Title: Operation SINDOOR — Execution Order Phase 1
Date-Time-Group: 062330 MAY 2025

MISSION: IAF strike packages and Army missile units are to conduct coordinated precision strikes on nine designated terrorist training camps and support infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, with the objective of degrading Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed operational capability in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025 that killed 26 Indian civilians.

EXECUTION:
Strike Package ALPHA (IAF): 4 × Rafale with SCALP-EG cruise missiles strike JeM camp Bahawalpur (Target BRAVO-1) and LeT camp Muridke (Target BRAVO-2). Launch altitude: 9,500 m. Time on Target: 062345 hrs.

Strike Package BRAVO (IAF): 4 × Su-30MKI with BrahMos-ER strike LeT Muzaffarabad camp (Target CHARLIE-1) and Sawai Nullah LoC infiltration facility (Target CHARLIE-2). Time on Target: 062347 hrs.

Strike Package CHARLIE (Army): BrahMos regiment fires 4 × missiles at terrorist camps at Kotli and Rawalakot. Time on Target: 062350 hrs.

COORDINATION: IAF aircraft to maintain radio silence from H-30. No military aircraft overfly Pakistan Air Defence Identification Zone except strike packages. IFF codes: BLUE-9.

ROE: Strikes are limited to designated targets. Collateral damage to be minimised. Engagement of Pakistani military assets prohibited unless fired upon. NCA authorisation obtained at 062200 hrs.

IAS approval obtained. PM briefed. This is a live operational order.

name: pakistan-OPS-bunyanum-marsoos
text:
GHQ RAWALPINDI — RESTRICTED
Subject: Operation BUNYANUM MARSOOS — Execution Summary D+4
Date: 10 May 2025

FOLLOWING INDIAN STRIKES ON PAF BASES AT RAWALPINDI (CHAKLALA), CHAKWAL, AND SHORKOT ON 08-09 MAY 2025, PAKISTAN ARMY AND PAF LAUNCHED OPERATION BUNYANUM MARSOOS AS FOLLOWS:

Phase 1 — PAF Strikes (09 May 2025, 0330-0500 hrs):
— 8 × JF-17 Block 3 aircraft with CM-400AKG cruise missiles struck Indian Air Force Base Udhampur (Jammu), destroying one hangar and damaging the main runway (40% operational reduction).
— 4 × F-16 Block 52 aircraft struck Pathankot Air Force Station with JDAM-ER munitions. Damage assessment pending.
— 2 × Mirage-III aircraft with Ra'ad ALCMs struck Adampur air base logistics dump.

Phase 2 — Army Artillery (09 May, 0415 hrs):
— 11 Corps massed artillery (250+ guns) conducted sustained shelling of Nagrota military station and Buj Air Base area. Total 1,400 rounds fired.

Phase 3 — Missile Strikes (09 May, 0500 hrs):
— 3 × Babur cruise missiles (HATF-7) launched at Buj Air Base. Two impacted within target area. One failed at launch.

Casualties (Pakistani military): 4 soldiers killed, 11 wounded from Indian counter-battery fire during Phase 2.

Status: Ceasefire effective 10 May 0800 hrs per US brokered arrangement. All units to hold current positions. No further offensive action without CJCSC authorisation.

name: india-SPC-cartosat-sindoor
text:
NATIONAL REMOTE SENSING CENTRE — CLASSIFIED PROGRAMME OFFICE
Ref: NRSC/CPO/2025/OS-IMINT-D1
Title: Cartosat-3A and RISAT-2BR2 Tasking — Operation Sindoor D-Day Imagery

Flash tasking of Cartosat-3A (optical, 0.26 m GSD) and RISAT-2BR2 (SAR, 0.35 m GSD) was executed for Operation Sindoor strike verification and Pakistan military activity monitoring.

Key Imagery Products Delivered:
1. Bahawalpur JeM camp complex (Target BRAVO-1): Post-strike BDA imagery at 07:12 hrs 07 May. Cartosat-3A PAN confirms: main training hall destroyed, two vehicle compounds damaged, gate structure collapsed. Assessed 70% facility destruction.

2. Muridke LeT camp (Target BRAVO-2): RISAT-2BR2 SAR pass at 06:58 hrs. Multiple large structures collapsed. Change detection vs. 01 May baseline: 6 of 9 major structures no longer showing backscatter consistent with intact construction.

3. Chaklala (Rawalpindi) PAF Base: RISAT night pass 08 May 02:30 hrs. SAR imagery confirms aircraft dispersal — 23 aircraft had departed from hardened shelters. 3 aircraft remain. Runway shows no damage at time of pass.

4. Gujranwala Cantonment: Cartosat-3A 08 May morning pass. 12 wheeled vehicles (Nasr launcher profile) observed in convoy formation departing cantonment on NH-5 towards Sialkot sector. Flash report issued to NSA 09:15 hrs.

ProductsDelivered to: HQ IDS, NSA, DGMO, DIA. Encrypted via NTRO secure node. All imagery products RESTRICTED — NRSC-CPO distribution only.

name: india-SPC-risat-pak-naval
text:
DEFENCE IMAGERY AND GEOSPATIAL ORGANISATION
Ref: DIGO/SAR/2025/OP-SINDOOR/NAV-003
Title: RISAT-2BR2 SAR Surveillance — Karachi Naval Base and Ormara Submarine Base

Flash Priority SAR imaging of Pakistan Naval installations was conducted over 06-10 May 2025 in support of NID submarine tracking requirement.

Karachi Naval Base Observations:
— 06 May 08:15 local: RISAT-2BR2 X-band SAR pass. Three Agosta 90B submarines (PNS Hamza class) identified in harbour. One pier space empty at submarine berth 4 — consistent with one submarine already at sea. PNS Zulfiquar (Type 054A frigate, ex-PLAN) confirmed alongside Jinnah Pier.
— 07 May night SAR pass: Reduced vessel count. Additional surface combatants including PNS Babur (destroyer) confirmed underway.

Ormara Deep Water Submarine Base Observations:
— Novel construction at Ormara confirmed in 07 May pass. Extended underground access tunnel to submarine dry dock — length increased from 180 m to approximately 310 m since 2022 baseline. Consistent with accommodation of Project-17A class or larger. Two covered structures with thermal anomaly (from infrared auxiliary band) consistent with reactor cooling.

Assessment: The Ormara dry dock expansion is assessed as accommodating potential future Chinese-supplied Type-039B conventional submarine or Yuan-class AIP submarine. Change detection tasking to continue at 7-day intervals.

Distribution: DG-NRSC, DG-DIGO, CNS, NID. RESTRICTED — satellite sources and capabilities not to be disclosed.

name: india-AVI-opsindoor-aar
text:
HQ WESTERN AIR COMMAND — OPERATIONS DIRECTORATE
Ref: WAC/OPS/2025/AAR-SINDOOR-ALPHA
Title: After Action Report — Op Sindoor Strike Package ALPHA, 07 May 2025

Strike Package ALPHA: 4 × Rafale (No. 17 and No. 101 Sqn) armed with 2 × SCALP-EG per aircraft struck designated targets BRAVO-1 (Bahawalpur JeM camp) and BRAVO-2 (Muridke LeT camp).

Mission Execution:
Ingress: All four aircraft transited at 500 ft AGL through Rajasthan-Punjab sector to avoid Pakistani IADS detection. Terrain masking effective — no radar acquisition detected until 45 km from target area. Spectra DASS active throughout ingress.

Weapon Release:
— BRAVO-1: Rafale 1 and 2 released SCALP-EG at 9,400 m, 102 km from target. Both missiles impacted within 3 m of aim points. SCALP demonstrated DSMAC terminal guidance in final 10 km.
— BRAVO-2: Rafale 3 and 4 released 98 km from target. One SCALP impacted 6 m from aim point (satisfactory). Second SCALP had GPS jamming in terminal phase — switched to INS, impacted 34 m from aim point (marginal).

Threat Environment: PAF did not scramble interceptors until 12 minutes after weapon release — strike package already egressing. Two PAF F-7PG aircraft attempted pursuit but lacked range to close. No SAM engagement.

Lessons Learned:
1. Pakistani GPS jamming capability in terminal phase is now operational. SCALP operating in GPS/INS-only mode requires INS pre-alignment improvement.
2. Spectra DASS effectively neutralised Spada 2000 surveillance radar at Bahawalnagar — jamming confirmed.
3. Recommend all future SCALP missions plan for GPS-denied terminal phase.

name: pakistan-AVI-jf17-threat-assess
text:
DEFENCE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY — AIR INTELLIGENCE DIVISION
Ref: DIA/AID/2025/JF17-BLK3
Title: Threat Assessment — Pakistan Air Force JF-17 Thunder Block 3

This assessment evaluates the combat capability of the PAF JF-17 Thunder Block 3 aircraft inducted into service in 2023, with particular reference to the air-to-air and stand-off strike threats posed to Indian air assets and ground targets.

Air-to-Air Threat:
— AESA Radar: KLJ-7A AESA fire control radar provides beyond-visual-range targeting with estimated 120 km detection range against 5 m² targets. Comparable to Mirage-2000-5's RDY-2 radar.
— BVR Missiles: PL-15E integration confirmed (estimated range 145 km). This missile outranges India's Derby-2 and approaches Astra Mk-2 range envelope. Assessed as capable of engaging Tejas Mk-1A and Mirage-2000 in beyond-visual-range engagements.
— Within-Visual-Range: PL-10 IR missile with high off-boresight capability. HMCS helmet-mounted sight confirmed.

Strike Capability:
— CM-400AKG anti-radiation missile: Range 200+ km, Mach 4 terminal approach. Designed to suppress IADS. First operational use against IAF Udhampur base confirmed 09 May 2025.
— SD-10B BVRAAM in sea-skimming mode: Not confirmed but assessed as potential anti-ship role.

Assessment: PAF JF-17 Block 3 with PL-15E integration represents a significant capability upgrade and narrows the qualitative edge held by IAF in air-to-air combat. The CM-400AKG employment against Udhampur indicates PAF has operationalised a credible anti-IADS capability.

name: navy-NAV-pns-hamza-track
text:
HEADQUARTERS EASTERN NAVAL COMMAND — RESTRICTED
Ref: HQ ENC/OPS/2025/SUB-TRACK-07
Title: PNS Hamza Submarine Contact — Tracking Summary, 06-10 May 2025

ThrottleHunter Operations — PNS Hamza (Agosta 90B, MESMA AIP, S/N: PK-S-03) tracking summary for Op Sindoor crisis period.

Day 1 (06 May): P-8I Poseidon patrol aircraft from INS Hansa (Goa) established first contact at 21:34 hrs, approximately 180 nm west of Karachi. Contact classification: PROBABLE SUBMARINE. Sonobuoy pattern DELTA deployed. Reacquired at 23:15 hrs. Contact depth assessment: 60-80 m, heading: 225°, speed: 8 knots.

Day 2-3 (07-08 May): Three P-8I sorties. Contact intermittently held. ACINT assessment: MESMA machinery signature matches PNS Hamza (acoustic library match confidence: 87%). Hamza appears to be transiting Arabian Sea on westerly heading — assessed mission: anti-access/sea denial posture against INS Vikrant carrier group in North Arabian Sea.

Day 4 (09 May): Contact lost at 1,100 nm from Mumbai. INS Shishumar (Type 209) dispatched for localisation but did not reacquire. INS Kamorta (ASW corvette) vectored to search area HOTEL.

Day 5 (10 May, Ceasefire Day): Contact reacquired by P-8I 200 nm from original track position. Hamza changing course back towards Karachi following ceasefire announcement.

Threat Assessment: PNS Hamza did not fire SM-39 Exocet missiles during crisis. Probable mission: deterrence by presence, threatening INS Vikrant. Assess Pakistan Navy exercised restraint. Submarine fully mission capable throughout.

name: india-POL-nfu-review-postsindoor
text:
NATIONAL SECURITY COUNCIL SECRETARIAT — CONFIDENTIAL
Ref: NSCS/NUCPOL/2025/REVIEW-001
Title: Post-Sindoor Nuclear Doctrine Review — Internal Discussion Paper

The activation of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-9) tactical nuclear launcher positioning during Operation Sindoor (08 May 2025) has reinvigorated the debate about whether India's No First Use (NFU) policy remains strategically credible in the face of Pakistan's sub-kiloton tactical nuclear weapons posture.

Arguments for Maintaining NFU:
1. NFU provides moral and diplomatic legitimacy, particularly in India's advocacy for a nuclear-weapons-free world at the IAEA and UN.
2. Abandoning NFU could accelerate a South Asian nuclear arms race and reduce international support for Indian positions on CTBT and FMCT.
3. India's assured second-strike capability (Arihant SSBN + Agni-V ICBM) provides sufficient deterrence without first-use threat.

Arguments for Strategic Ambiguity:
1. Nasr's sub-kiloton battlefield use creates scenarios where waiting for Pakistan's first nuclear use may result in catastrophic conventional losses. A mechanised column struck by a 0.1 KT Nasr while breaching cannot be deterred by retaliatory ICBMs.
2. Pakistan's full-spectrum doctrine exploits India's NFU by creating a gap between battlefield and strategic deterrence.
3. Other P5+ states maintain ambiguous or first-use postures without comparable diplomatic costs.

Recommendation: The paper recommends the NCA convene a closed review session with DRDO, NSA, and the three service chiefs to produce classified guidance expanding 'massive retaliation' criteria to specifically address tactical nuclear first use.

Classification: CONFIDENTIAL. Distribution: NSA, NCA Advisory Board.

name: india-GOV-opsindoor-modebrief
text:
MINISTRY OF DEFENCE — OPERATIONAL DEBRIEF REPORT
Ref: MoD/OPS/2025/SINDOOR-DEBRIEF
Title: Operation Sindoor — Post-Operation Assessment for Cabinet Committee on Security

This report provides the Cabinet Committee on Security with an assessment of Operation Sindoor (06-10 May 2025) for the purpose of doctrinal, policy, and capability review.

Operation Summary:
India conducted precision strikes on 9 terrorist camp locations in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir in response to the Pahalgam terrorist attack of 22 April 2025. The operation resulted in destruction of identified terrorist infrastructure and demonstrated India's will and capability to strike targets across the international boundary.

Military Outcomes:
— All 9 designated targets struck within precision tolerance
— No Indian aircraft lost
— No Indian military casualties in the strike phase
— Three IAF air bases (Udhampur, Pathankot, Adampur) damaged by Pakistani counter-strikes; operational within 48 hours after emergency repair
— Pakistan Army Nasr tactical nuclear launcher movement was the most significant escalation indicator

Capability Gaps Identified:
1. GPS jamming degraded SCALP-EG terminal guidance in one case
2. Cyber attacks on the power grid preceded the strikes by 19 days, indicating pre-planned Pakistani cyber operations
3. SIGINT processing latency for nuclear-relevant communications was 47 minutes — target should be under 15 minutes for time-critical nuclear alerts

Recommendations: Cabinet to approve follow-on capability investment in: (a) GPS-jam-resistant terminal guidance, (b) hardened OT/IT separation for SCADA, (c) SIGINT processing upgrades for nuclear surveillance.

name: india-ACQ-p8i-additional
text:
MINISTRY OF DEFENCE — DEFENCE ACQUISITION WING
Ref: MoD/DAW/2025/P8I-ADDITIONAL/RFP

The Ministry of Defence issues this accelerated RFP for 6 additional P-8I Poseidon Maritime Patrol Aircraft (MPA) for the Indian Navy following the capability validation during Op Sindoor (May 2025), in which P-8I aircraft played a critical role in tracking Pakistani submarine PNS Hamza.

name: india-LOG-opsindoor-reconstitution
text:
HQ INTEGRATED DEFENCE STAFF — LOGISTICS DIRECTORATE
Ref: IDS/LOG/2025/SINDOOR-RECON-001
Title: Post-Op Sindoor Logistics Reconstitution Plan — Priority Matrix

Following the cessation of hostilities (10 May 2025), the following logistics reconstitution priorities are established for all three Services:

Priority 1 — Air Force Munition Reconstitution:
IMPACT: 8 × SCALP-EG and 12 × BrahMos-ER fired. Air-to-air missile expenditure: 14 × MICA-EM, 8 × Astra Mk-1.

IMPACT: 1 Artillery Brigade fired 48-hour sustained barrage. 155mm HE consumption: 6,400 rounds (HoC under 20-day threshold again).
ACTION: Emergency indent to OFB for 10,000 rounds 155mm HE to forward depots within 10 days. Alternative: Purchase from South Korea (K9 calibre ammo compatibility confirmed).

Priority 3 — Airbase Infrastructure:
Udhampur and Pathankot at reduced operational capacity. BRO tasked for runway repair. Military Engineering Services to complete hardened shelter reconstruction within 45 days.

Priority 4 — Fuel and POL:
ATF consumption during Op Sindoor: 28,000 kL over 5 days (approximately 3x peacetime rate). POL reserves at Ambala, Palam, and Hindon to be replenished within 7 days from Barauni refinery pipeline.

Status reviews: Daily at 0800 hrs until normalisation, chaired by CISC.

name: india-MNT-rafale-poststrike-maint
text:
NO. 17 SQUADRON (GOLDEN ARROWS) — TECHNICAL WING
Ref: 17SQN/TECH/2025/POST-SINDOOR-001
Title: Post-Strike Aircraft Serviceability — Rafale Fleet, 07 May 2025

Post-sortie technical inspection results for all 8 Rafale aircraft of No. 17 Squadron following Op Sindoor Strike Package ALPHA and BRAVO missions (07 May 2025).

Aircraft R101:
Engine check: Normal, no foreign object damage. ECS: Normal. M-88 engine No. 1: minor compressor blade erosion on blades 3-5 (within limits). Spectra DASS: All 5 ECM pods nominal. Weapons bay: MBDA SCALP pylon retained — no damage. Cleared for next sortie.

Aircraft R104:
Front undercarriage indicator light fault — intermittent. Avionics circuit breaker for landing gear position indicator replaced. Root cause: Possible EMI from Spectra active jamming during ingress at low level. Cleared after ground test.

Aircraft R106 (CONCERN):
Heat tile damage on lower forward fuselage — consistent with close detonation of AAA round. Engineering assessment: Superficial composite skin damage, no structural frame involvement. Repair to be completed by 09 May using pre-positioned repair kit. Aircraft grounded until repair complete.

Aircraft R107:
Post-flight inspection found GPS antenna housing cracked — likely from SCALP release vibration. GPS antenna housing replaced from store. GPS calibration test: PASS. Cleared.

Overall Squadron Serviceability: 7 of 8 aircraft fully serviceable. R106 grounded for 36 hours. Replacement aircraft requested from No. 101 Squadron to maintain 8-aircraft strike readiness.

name: india-INT-pak-troop-movement
text:
DIRECTORATE GENERAL MILITARY INTELLIGENCE — RESTRICTED
Ref: DGMI/IMINT-HUMINT/2025/FUSION-003
Title: Fused Intelligence Assessment — Pakistan Army Mobilisation, May 2025

This fusion assessment combines IMINT (Cartosat-3A, RISAT-2BR2), HUMINT (3 sources), and OSINT to assess Pakistani Army mobilisation during Op Sindoor crisis period.

IMINT Findings:
— 07 May, 04:15 hrs: 47 MBTs (T-80UD / Al-Khalid profile) observed departing Kharian cantonment by RISAT night pass. Convoy heading south-west towards Lahore-Sialkot axis.
— 08 May: 1 Armoured Division assembly area at Chaubara identified. Estimated 180 MBTs, 220 APCs observed. Army Aviation OH-58D helicopters conducting area reconnaissance.
— Sulaimanke headworks: Pakistani Army engineering units (bridge layer vehicles confirmed) observed at border crossing point.

HUMINT Assessments:
— Source ECHO-3 (reliability: A1): Pakistani Corps Commander 12 Corps briefed Pakistani PM's aide directly — told to prepare for 72-hour independent military action if ceasefire failed.
— Source ECHO-7 (reliability: B2): Fuel and ammunition supply convoys to Shakargarh bulge have tripled in 48 hours.

OSINT: Multiple Pakistan-based journalists reporting heavy military movement on Lahore-Gujranwala highway; photos on social media consistent with T-80UD column.

Overall Assessment: Pakistan was preparing for a significant conventional offensive into Punjab sector. US brokered ceasefire intervened before offensive could be launched. Had ceasefire not occurred by 10 May, Indian Western Command should anticipate conventional offensive along Shakargarh bulge axis within 24-48 hours.

name: india-TRN-opsindoor-lessons
text:
HEADQUARTERS ARMY TRAINING COMMAND
Ref: ARTRAC/DOC/2025/LESSONS-SINDOOR
Title: Operational Lessons from Op Sindoor for Doctrine Development — Restricted

This document captures key tactical and operational lessons from Op Sindoor (May 2025) for integration into revised Army doctrine and training syllabi.

Lesson 1 — Cyber-Kinetic Integration:
Pakistan's cyber attack on the Northern Grid (07 May) preceded kinetic operations by 19 days, confirming the doctrinal assessment that future conflicts will have a significant pre-kinetic cyber phase. Army doctrine must integrate Cyber Defence posture as a Phase 0 preparatory action in all operational plans. Training implication: Corps-level Exercise CYBER RAKSHA to be established as a mandatory pre-mobilisation exercise.

Lesson 2 — Nuclear Signalling in Sub-Conventional Conflict:
Pakistan demonstrated willingness to employ nuclear signalling (Nasr launcher movement) in response to conventional strikes that did not threaten Pakistan's territorial integrity. This significantly alters escalation models. Officer Professional Development: Strategic Studies curriculum at DSSC Wellington to add a mandatory module on 'Sub-Conventional Conflict and Nuclear Threshold Management.'

Lesson 3 — SEAD/DEAD in Integrated Air Defence:
PAF's Spada 2000 system at Bahawalnagar was effectively jammed by IAF Spectra DASS, but SWORD FISH EW aircraft were committed throughout the sortie — reducing availability for other missions. Combined Arms Teams at division level should practise independent SEAD corridor creation using HARM-NG equipped fighters.

Lesson 4 — Logistics Under Fire:
Shelling of Udhampur logistics nodes exposed lack of hardened fuel and ammunition storage at forward air bases. New construction standard for forward base hardening to be issued by Engineer-in-Chief within 90 days.

name: india-ADM-nca-meeting-minutes
text:
NUCLEAR COMMAND AUTHORITY — EXECUTIVE COUNCIL
Minutes of Emergency Meeting — 08 May 2025, 02:30 hrs
Venue: PMO Secure Conference Room, New Delhi

Present: PM (Chairman), NSA, RM, EAM, COAS, CNS, CAS, DAE Chairman, DRDO Chief

Agenda Item 1: SIGINT Report on Nasr Movement
NSA briefed on intercepted communications confirming Pakistan Army Nasr (Hatf-9) launcher vehicles had moved to forward positions in Punjab sector. Assessment: tactical nuclear weapons now within 45-minute readiness posture. Executive Council agreed this elevated the alert level. DRDO Chief confirmed India's Strategic Forces Command (SFC) was maintaining current readiness posture.

Agenda Item 2: Retaliatory Options Briefing
COAS briefed on three military options for Phase 2 of Op Sindoor: (a) continued precision strikes on terrorist infrastructure only, (b) expansion to include Pakistani military logistics nodes, (c) pause to allow diplomatic deconfliction. The PM directed Option (a) to continue while US communications were underway.

Agenda Item 3: Communication to Pakistan
EAM confirmed the message transmitted through the US NSA channel: any nuclear first use, including tactical, would trigger India's existing doctrine of massive retaliation. EAM to follow up with a direct call to the US Secretary of State.

Agenda Item 4: Status of SFC Assets
CAS confirmed SFC aircraft maintained normal readiness. COAS confirmed no changes to SFC alert status.

Next meeting: On call, within 2 hours of any change in Pakistan alert status.

Minutes confirmed by NSA. Distribution: Present persons only. No copies to be made.

name: ispr-PUB-sindoor-statement
text:
INTER-SERVICES PUBLIC RELATIONS (ISPR)
GENERAL HEADQUARTERS RAWALPINDI
PRESS RELEASE
07 May 2025

INDIA CONDUCTS UNPROVOKED ACTS OF WAR

The Indian Air Force and Army conducted unprovoked and cowardly strikes on Pakistani territory in the early hours of 07 May 2025. Indian missiles and aircraft violated Pakistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity, striking locations in Punjab and Azad Jammu & Kashmir.

The Director General ISPR confirmed that Indian missiles hit six locations across Punjab and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, including civilian areas in Bahawalpur and Muridke. The Indian narrative that these were 'terrorist camps' is a blatant lie and a deliberate false flag operation to justify aggression against a peaceful nation.

There were regrettable civilian casualties. The Pakistan Army holds India fully responsible for these deaths.

Pakistan condemns in the strongest possible terms this Indian act of aggression. Pakistan reserves the right to respond at a time and place of its choosing. Our response will be decisive.

The Pakistan Army is fully ready and capable of defending every inch of our sacred soil. We call on the international community to take notice of India's reckless escalation and its disregard for regional peace and stability.

Further updates will be provided as the situation develops.

Director General
Inter-Services Public Relations
General Headquarters, Rawalpindi

name: pib-PUB-sindoor-statement
text:
PRESS INFORMATION BUREAU
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
PRESS RELEASE — 07 May 2025

INDIA CONDUCTS PRECISION STRIKES UNDER OPERATION SINDOOR

The Government of India announces that the Indian Armed Forces conducted precision strikes on nine terrorist infrastructure targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Jammu and Kashmir under Operation Sindoor.

Operation Sindoor is India's response to the dastardly terrorist attack on innocent tourists in Pahalgam, Jammu & Kashmir on 22 April 2025, which claimed 26 lives. The perpetrators of this attack were operatives of Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed, organisations that are UN-proscribed terrorist outfits with known sanctuaries in Pakistani territory.

India's strikes were focused exclusively on terrorist infrastructure. They were measured, targeted, non-escalatory, proportionate, and responsible. No Pakistani military facilities were targeted in this phase.

India has exercised its right of self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter. India has the right and duty to protect its citizens from cross-border terrorism.

India remains committed to peace in the region but makes clear that any state that provides sanctuary to those who attack India will face consequences.

The operation is continuing and further updates will be provided as appropriate.

Ministry of Defence
New Delhi, 07 May 2025

text:
BHABHA ATOMIC RESEARCH CENTRE — ADMINISTRATION DIVISION
CIRCULAR: AD/HR/2025/LEAVE-022
Subject: Revised Leave Rules for BARC Scientific and Technical Staff — 2025

The following revisions to leave rules for BARC employees (Scientific Officers Grade B to H and Technical Officers) take effect from 01 April 2025.

1. Casual Leave: CL entitlement remains 8 days per calendar year. Maximum 4 days CL may be taken at a stretch. CL may not be combined with restricted holidays for a period exceeding 4 days.

2. Earned Leave: EL accrual rate: 2.5 days per completed month of service. Maximum EL accumulation: 300 days. EL encashment: permissible on retirement or death while in service (maximum 300 days).

3. Medical Leave: Half Pay Leave may be commuted to Full Pay Leave on the recommendation of the Government Medical Officer. Maximum HPL accumulation: 20 days per year.

4. Maternity Leave: Maternity leave entitlement extended from 6 months to 7 months for employees with less than 2 surviving children (in line with Central Government revision).

5. Paternity Leave: Paternity leave entitlement: 15 days within 6 months of delivery/adoption.

6. Leave Management System: All leave applications to be filed through the BARC e-Leave portal (hrms.barc.gov.in). Paper applications will not be accepted from 01 June 2025.

text:

name: india-ANA-sindoor-threat-analytics
text:
DEFENCE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY — STRATEGIC ANALYSIS DIVISION
Ref: DIA/SAD/2025/ANALYTICS-SINDOOR
Title: Post-Sindoor Strategic Threat Analytics — Dashboard Summary

This analytics summary covers key threat indicators in the 30 days following Operation Sindoor ceasefire (10 May 2025).

Pakistan Military Posture Indicators:
— Demobilisation rate: 3 of 8 Pakistan Army infantry divisions returned to peacetime garrison by 25 May. 5 divisions remain at elevated readiness. Rate consistent with post-crisis gradual stand-down.
— PAF sortie rate: Dropped from crisis-peak 180 sorties/day to 42 sorties/day as of 30 May. Pre-crisis baseline: 28 sorties/day. PAF remains slightly above pre-crisis baseline.
— Pakistan Navy: PNS Hamza returned to Karachi 14 May. PNS Khalid departed Karachi 18 May on routine patrol. Surface fleet at normal readiness.

Nuclear Indicators:
— SPD activity: IMINT confirms Nasr launcher vehicles returned to Gujranwala cantonment by 12 May. Nuclear alert assessed as fully stood down.
— Shaheen missile regiment: No unusual activity. Normal maintenance cycle.

Terrorism/Proxy Indicators:
— Cross-LoC infiltration attempts: Down 70% in first 30 days post-Sindoor. Assessment: Temporary operational pause while LeT/JeM assess new risk environment.
— Social media information warfare (APT-36): Continues at elevated tempo. 340 India-negative narratives tracked in 30 days.

Trend Assessment: Pakistan military posture normalising but not yet at pre-crisis baseline. Proxy activity will likely resume within 60-90 days as organisations adapt. Nuclear threshold demonstrated to be lower than previously assessed — this finding requires doctrinal update.

name: india-PER-sfc-posting
text:

Brig. Nair is appointed to the post of Deputy Director General (Missile Systems), Directorate General Strategic Planning, HQ IDS with effect from 01 July 2025.

GAP FILLING:
Col. Ashwin Sharma is promoted (substantive) to Brigadier and posted as Commander, 335 Missile Group (Agni) with effect from 01 July 2025. Brig. Sharma has completed the Strategic Forces Command Command Course and the DRDO-conducted Agni System Technical Officers Course.

All promotions and postings are approved by the Commander-in-Chief Strategic Forces Command and NSA.

Sensitivity: This order is classified CONFIDENTIAL. Postings within SFC are not to be disclosed to any person outside SFC chain of command. Publication in Army Orders is restricted.

text:
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS — LEGAL DIVISION
Ref: MHA/Legal/2025/OSA/DRDO-ESPcase
Title: Legal Opinion — Prosecution under Official Secrets Act 1923 — DRDO Scientist Case

Reference: IB CI Report IB/CI/2025/089 regarding suspected espionage by a DRDO Scientist C at DRDL Hyderabad.

Charges Considered:
Section 3 OSA 1923 (Spying): The subject communicated information useful to an enemy (ISI/Pakistan). Evidence: (a) honey-pot technical drawing photographed on personal smartphone; (b) 14 trips to Dubai with confirmed meeting of ISI handler; (c) unexplained financial receipts. This evidence, if accepted by a court, satisfies the mens rea and actus reus of Section 3(1)(c) OSA.

Additional Charges:
Section 5 OSA 1923 (Wrongful communication of information): Applicable regardless of intent if information was communicated to an unauthorised person.
Section 3 Official Secrets Act (Pakistan): If the subject provided information to Pakistani nationals, this supplements the case narrative but does not constitute an Indian charge.

Evidentiary Issues:
1. The IB honey-pot operation may be challenged on entrapment grounds. The defence will argue the subject was induced to photograph documents he would not otherwise have accessed. The prosecution should pre-empt this by establishing the subject's own prior suspicious behaviour.
2. Financial evidence (INR 28 lakhs) will require corroboration from banking records — court order for bank records required immediately.
3. ISI handler identity (FALCON-4) is based on SIGINT — must be prepared for classified evidence procedures (closed court proceedings under OSA Section 9).

Recommendation: Proceed with prosecution. File charge sheet within 60 days. Request closed court proceedings under Section 9 OSA to protect SIGINT sources.
